steps.hints: ❓ Did you type quotation marks around the string inside the parentheses of game.splash(text)?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What symbol needs to surround a string in JavaScript, in order for the code to run correctly?


Solution: 

Quotation marks should be added to the string arguments, so that the code reads: game.splash(“Time for...”, “the show!”)
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the splash screen that says “Time for...the show!” appears when the project starts.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 2 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about properties and code comments. In JavaScript, you can type directly on the editor to organize your code using code comments and set different sprite properties. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 2:

badges.title: Parameter Pilot
badges.description: Use the JavaScript editor’s documentation and code completion tools when adding parameters to functions.

badges.title: Comment, Like, and Subscribe
badges.description: Add a comment to your code.

badges.title: Say What Now?
badges.description: Use the sayText function with all 5 parameters.

badges.title: Stop and Smell the Roses
badges.description: Use the pause function to temporarily stop your project from running new code.

badges.title: Effective Immediately
badges.description: Use the startScreenEffect function with 2 parameters.

badges.title: Music to My Ears
badges.description: Use the play function to play a melody.

badges.title: To Whom it May Concern
badges.description: Use the splash function to display a message on screen.

badges.title: A Speedy Recovery
